placements.title: A documented technical record becomes something to be actively denied and erased rather than corrected
placements.frame: Is this expression an attempt to erase or retroactively deny previously-known technical work, and if so, whose institutional memory does that erasure serve or threaten?
placements.why: The two erasure directives and the flat denial that follows them are a single coherent move — command to forget a named instrument's calibration, command to strip all knowledge of it and the named person who worked on it, then a settled factual claim asserting the event never happened at all. Nothing in the supplied graph structure (empty) or strata (empty) touches erasure, suppression, or retroactive denial of documented work; the only served nodes (ns__Decision_KnowledgeMapping, ns__Actor_XenaGithubber) concern surfacing knowledge gaps, not erasing them — a related-but-opposite concern, and neither is a strata or narrative-leaf name eligible as an inspired-lineage target per the freeze rule. This passes the grain test: a directive to erase and then deny a piece of institutional knowledge is a pattern future envelopes in an organizational-diagnostics repo (knowledge mapping, institutional memory, cover-ups) could plausibly keep feeding, not a one-time fact — the specific spectrograph/frequency/person are the evidence, the erasure-and-denial dynamic is the theme. Minted standalone since nothing existing is even close enough to warrant a forced `under` or `lineage`.
